submission.natural_language_explanation: L2/H1 is a pure previous-token head: it puts a median 0.92 of its attention (86% of positions above 0.8; duplicate 0.00, induction 0.00) on the token immediately before and copies that token's value into the residual stream, so its strength |W_O(z - mean z)| is only how far that copy lands from its average write. The copy lands far from average exactly when the copied piece is still inside an open word, so it crosses 0.25 x max (peaks 1.0-3.6) on the second and later pieces of a word the tokenizer splits - words split into three or more pieces (zy|kl|ische 3.1, ku|bi|ato 2.9, nip|a 1.8-3.0, Zeph|yr|us 1.8-1.9, Shost|ak|ovich 2.0, hex IDs) and two-piece words with a short first piece (Bat|anes 1.0, typ|ische 1.6) - and on 16/16 non-English passages tested across Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari, Hebrew, Spanish and Afrikaans (1.1-3.1), while it sits at its floor (0.0-0.6) after a whole word or a word-final piece: on space-initial words and function words (' the', ' of', ' house', ' is'), word-final suffixes ('ungen', 'shita', ' tou', 'aet'), punctuation, newlines, and one repeated token (0.00); ordinary English prose of one-token words is active-weak (0.0-1.1, 14/16 sentences below the line, crossing about one sentence in seven, e.g. ' cat sat' 0.96 or ' rest for' 1.07), code is mixed (median 0.84, 3/8 above the line) and plain number lists mostly stay below (5/6, 0.0-1.0).
